/-!
# What one counting-sort pass computes, as pure Lean

Nothing in this file mentions the extracted Rust. It is the half of the proof a
competition would pay for *once*, in the substrate, and `Sort/Refine.lean` is the
half a miner would pay per patch. Keeping them in separate files is how this
experiment measures the two costs separately -- which is the number that decides
whether the competition in `docs/RECOMMENDATION.md` can work.

The central choice here is to describe a pass by **where each source element
lands** rather than by a list-valued function of the source. `posAt` below is
"the start of my bucket, plus how many earlier elements share my digit". That
turns every obligation into index arithmetic -- `omega`'s territory -- and avoids
reasoning about list segments under `List.set`, which is where a bucket-concatenation
formulation spends most of its lines.
-/

namespace RadixSort

/-- The radix. Not `variable`-generalised: the extracted code has 256 baked in as
an array size, and pretending otherwise would only add casts. -/
def R : Nat := 256

variable {α : Type}

/-- How many of the first `j` elements have digit `b`. -/
def cnt (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b j : Nat) : Nat :=
  (xs.take j).countP (fun s => d s == b)

/-- How many elements have digit `b`; the histogram the first loop builds. -/
def total (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) : Nat :=
  xs.countP (fun s => d s == b)

/-- Where bucket `b` begins; the prefix sum the second loop builds. -/
def start (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) : Nat :=
  ∑ c ∈ Finset.range b, total d xs c

/-- Where the element at source index `j`, whose digit is `b`, is written. -/
def posAt (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b j : Nat) : Nat :=
  start d xs b + cnt d xs b j

@[simp] theorem cnt_zero (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) :
    cnt d xs b 0 = 0 := by simp [cnt]

theorem cnt_length (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) :
    cnt d xs b xs.length = total d xs b := by simp [cnt, total]

theorem cnt_of_length_le (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) {j : Nat}
    (h : xs.length ≤ j) : cnt d xs b j = total d xs b := by
  simp [cnt, total, List.take_of_length_le h]

/-- The step the histogram and scatter loops both take. -/
theorem cnt_succ (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b j : Nat) (h : j < xs.length) :
    cnt d xs b (j + 1) = cnt d xs b j + (if d xs[j] = b then 1 else 0) := by
  rw [cnt, cnt, List.take_add_one, List.getElem?_eq_getElem h, Option.toList_some,
    List.countP_append, List.countP_singleton]
  simp

theorem cnt_mono (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) {j k : Nat} (h : j ≤ k) :
    cnt d xs b j ≤ cnt d xs b k :=
  (List.take_prefix_take_left h).sublist.countP_le

/-- At most `j` of the first `j` elements are in any one bucket. This is the bound
that keeps the histogram's `+ 1` from overflowing a `usize`. -/
theorem cnt_le_index (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b j : Nat) : cnt d xs b j ≤ j := by
  have h := List.countP_le_length (l := xs.take j) (p := fun s => d s == b)
  simp only [cnt, List.length_take] at *
  omega

theorem cnt_le_total (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b j : Nat) :
    cnt d xs b j ≤ total d xs b := by
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j xs.length with h | h
  · rw [← cnt_length]; exact cnt_mono d xs b (by omega)
  · rw [cnt_of_length_le d xs b h]

theorem start_succ (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (b : Nat) :
    start d xs (b + 1) = start d xs b + total d xs b :=
  Finset.sum_range_succ _ _

theorem start_mono (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) {b c : Nat} (h : b ≤ c) :
    start d xs b ≤ start d xs c :=
  Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset (by intro x hx; simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hx ⊢; omega)

/-- Every element falls in exactly one bucket, so the buckets exhaust the list.
This is what makes `start R = length`, and so what keeps every scatter write
inside the destination slice. -/
theorem start_R (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (hd : ∀ s ∈ xs, d s < R) :
    start d xs R = xs.length := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp [start, total]
  | cons s xs ih =>
    have hs : d s < R := hd s (by simp)
    have ih' := ih (fun t ht => hd t (by simp [ht]))
    have hone : ∑ c ∈ Finset.range R, (if d s = c then 1 else 0) = 1 := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq (Finset.range R) (d s) (fun _ => 1)]
      simp [Finset.mem_range, hs]
    simp only [start, total, List.countP_cons, beq_iff_eq] at *
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ih', hone]
    simp

theorem cnt_lt_total (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) {b j : Nat} (h : j < xs.length)
    (hb : d xs[j] = b) : cnt d xs b j < total d xs b := by
  have h1 := cnt_succ d xs b j h
  have h2 := cnt_le_total d xs b (j + 1)
  simp only [hb, if_pos] at h1
  omega

/-- Every write lands inside the destination. The bound is not incidental: it is
what makes the extracted `Slice.update` succeed rather than `fail`. -/
theorem posAt_lt (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) (hd : ∀ s ∈ xs, d s < R) {j : Nat}
    (h : j < xs.length) : posAt d xs (d xs[j]) j < xs.length := by
  have hb : d xs[j] < R := hd _ (List.getElem_mem h)
  have h1 : cnt d xs (d xs[j]) j < total d xs (d xs[j]) := cnt_lt_total d xs h rfl
  have h2 : start d xs (d xs[j] + 1) ≤ start d xs R := start_mono d xs (by omega)
  rw [start_succ] at h2
  rw [← start_R d xs hd]
  simp only [posAt]
  omega

/-- The pass is stable, and that is the whole reason a two-pass radix sort works:
`posAt` is strictly monotone in *digit first, source index second*. -/
theorem posAt_lt_posAt (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) {j k : Nat}
    (hj : j < xs.length) (hk : k < xs.length)
    (h : d xs[j] < d xs[k] ∨ (d xs[j] = d xs[k] ∧ j < k)) :
    posAt d xs (d xs[j]) j < posAt d xs (d xs[k]) k := by
  rcases h with hlt | ⟨heq, hjk⟩
  · have h1 : cnt d xs (d xs[j]) j < total d xs (d xs[j]) := cnt_lt_total d xs hj rfl
    have h2 : start d xs (d xs[j] + 1) ≤ start d xs (d xs[k]) := start_mono d xs (by omega)
    rw [start_succ] at h2
    simp only [posAt]
    omega
  · have h1 : cnt d xs (d xs[j]) (j + 1) = cnt d xs (d xs[j]) j + 1 := by
      rw [cnt_succ d xs _ j hj]; simp
    have h2 : cnt d xs (d xs[j]) (j + 1) ≤ cnt d xs (d xs[j]) k := cnt_mono d xs _ (by omega)
    rw [posAt, posAt, ← heq]
    omega

/-- Two different source indices never write to the same place. This is what makes
the scatter a permutation, and it is the only fact the destination-buffer
invariant needs beyond `posAt_lt`. -/
theorem posAt_ne (d : α → Nat) (xs : List α) {j k : Nat}
    (hj : j < xs.length) (hk : k < xs.length) (h : j ≠ k) :
    posAt d xs (d xs[j]) j ≠ posAt d xs (d xs[k]) k := by
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge j k with hlt | hge
  · rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (d xs[j]) (d xs[k]) with hd | hd | hd
    · exact Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hj hk (.inl hd))
    · exact Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hj hk (.inr ⟨hd, hlt⟩))
    · exact (Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hk hj (.inl hd))).symm
  · have hlt : k < j := by omega
    rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (d xs[k]) (d xs[j]) with hd | hd | hd
    · exact (Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hk hj (.inl hd))).symm
    · exact (Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hk hj (.inr ⟨hd, hlt⟩))).symm
    · exact Nat.ne_of_lt (posAt_lt_posAt d xs hj hk (.inl hd))

/-! ## What a pass is

`IsPass d src dst` says only *where each source element went*. That it is a
permutation, and sorted, and stable, are consequences -- proved once, here.
-/

/-- One stable counting-sort pass by digit `d`. -/
def IsPass (d : α → Nat) (src dst : List α) : Prop :=
  dst.length = src.length ∧
  ∀ (j : Nat) (_ : j < src.length), dst[posAt d src (d src[j]) j]? = some src[j]

/-- A list indexed through a permutation of its positions is a permutation of it.

Stated over `Fin l₁.length` on both sides to keep the two length casts out of the
proof; `List.ofFn_getElem` then closes each side. -/
theorem perm_of_bij {β : Type} {l₁ l₂ : List β} (hlen : l₁.length = l₂.length)
    (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin l₁.length))
    (hget : ∀ j : Fin l₁.length,
      l₂[((e j) : Fin l₁.length).val]'(by have := (e j).isLt; omega) = l₁[j.val]) :
    l₂.Perm l₁ := by
  have h3 : List.ofFn (fun j : Fin l₁.length =>
      l₂[j.val]'(by have := j.isLt; omega)) = l₂ := by
    apply List.ext_getElem (by simp [hlen])
    intro i h1 h2
    simp
  have h2 : List.ofFn ((fun j : Fin l₁.length =>
      l₂[j.val]'(by have := j.isLt; omega)) ∘ e) = l₁ := by
    apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
    intro i hi1 hi2
    simpa using hget ⟨i, hi2⟩
  have hp := (Equiv.Perm.ofFn_comp_perm e
    (fun j : Fin l₁.length => l₂[j.val]'(by have := j.isLt; omega))).symm
  rw [h3, h2] at hp
  exact hp

namespace IsPass

variable {d : α → Nat} {src dst : List α}

/-- The scatter map, as a function on positions. -/
private def F (d : α → Nat) (src : List α) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R) :
    Fin src.length → Fin src.length :=
  fun j => ⟨posAt d src (d src[j.val]) j.val, posAt_lt d src hd j.isLt⟩

private theorem F_injective (d : α → Nat) (src : List α) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R) :
    Function.Injective (F d src hd) := by
  intro a b hab
  by_contra hne
  exact posAt_ne d src a.isLt b.isLt (fun h => hne (Fin.ext h))
    (by simpa [F] using congrArg Fin.val hab)

/-- Every destination position is written, which is what lets the sortedness
argument travel backwards from a position to a source index. -/
theorem exists_source (_ : IsPass d src dst) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R)
    {p : Nat} (hp : p < src.length) :
    ∃ (j : Nat) (_ : j < src.length), posAt d src (d src[j]) j = p := by
  have hsurj := (Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mp (F_injective d src hd)
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hsurj ⟨p, hp⟩
  exact ⟨j.val, j.isLt, by simpa [F] using congrArg Fin.val hj⟩

theorem perm (h : IsPass d src dst) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R) : dst.Perm src := by
  refine perm_of_bij h.1.symm (Equiv.ofBijective (F d src hd)
    ⟨F_injective d src hd, (Finite.injective_iff_surjective).mp (F_injective d src hd)⟩) ?_
  intro j
  have := h.2 j.val j.isLt
  rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by rw [h.1]; exact posAt_lt d src hd j.isLt)] at this
  simpa [Equiv.ofBijective, F] using this

/-- The one fact everything else is read off: for any two destination positions in
order, their sources are ordered by digit, and by index when the digits are equal.

Sortedness is the first disjunct, stability the second, and the second is what the
next pass needs. -/
theorem mono (h : IsPass d src dst) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R)
    {p q : Nat} (hp : p < dst.length) (hq : q < dst.length) (hpq : p < q) :
    ∃ (j k : Nat) (hj : j < src.length) (hk : k < src.length),
      dst[p] = src[j] ∧ dst[q] = src[k] ∧
      (d src[j] < d src[k] ∨ (d src[j] = d src[k] ∧ j < k)) := by
  have hlen := h.1
  obtain ⟨j, hj, hjp⟩ := h.exists_source hd (p := p) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hkq⟩ := h.exists_source hd (p := q) (by omega)
  refine ⟨j, k, hj, hk, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have := h.2 j hj
    rw [hjp, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hp] at this
    exact Option.some_injective _ this
  · have := h.2 k hk
    rw [hkq, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hq] at this
    exact Option.some_injective _ this
  · rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (d src[j]) (d src[k]) with hlt | heq | hgt
    · exact .inl hlt
    · rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy j k with h1 | h1 | h1
      · exact .inr ⟨heq, h1⟩
      · exfalso
        have : posAt d src (d src[j]) j = posAt d src (d src[k]) k := by rw [heq, h1]
        omega
      · have := posAt_lt_posAt d src hk hj (.inr ⟨heq.symm, h1⟩)
        omega
    · have := posAt_lt_posAt d src hk hj (.inl hgt)
      omega

/-- Sorted by digit: the first disjunct of `mono`, read off. -/
theorem sorted (h : IsPass d src dst) (hd : ∀ s ∈ src, d s < R) :
    dst.Pairwise (fun a b => d a ≤ d b) := by
  rw [List.pairwise_iff_getElem]
  intro i j hi hj hij
  obtain ⟨j1, j2, hj1, hj2, e1, e2, hcase⟩ := h.mono hd hi hj hij
  rw [e1, e2]
  rcases hcase with hc | ⟨hc, _⟩ <;> omega

end IsPass

/-! ## The 16-bit key

Two passes suffice because a `u16` key has two base-256 digits. Everything below
is `omega`'s work once `digit` is unfolded; it is here rather than inline so the
refinement file never has to think about keys.
-/

/-- The `p`-th base-256 digit of `k`. -/
def digit (p k : Nat) : Nat := k / 256 ^ p % 256

theorem digit_lt (p k : Nat) : digit p k < R := by
  simp only [digit, R]
  omega

theorem le_of_digit_eq {k1 k2 : Nat} (h1 : k1 < 65536) (h2 : k2 < 65536)
    (hhi : digit 1 k1 = digit 1 k2) (hlo : digit 0 k1 ≤ digit 0 k2) : k1 ≤ k2 := by
  simp only [digit, pow_one, pow_zero, Nat.div_one] at *
  omega

theorem le_of_digit_lt {k1 k2 : Nat} (h1 : k1 < 65536) (h2 : k2 < 65536)
    (h : digit 1 k1 < digit 1 k2) : k1 ≤ k2 := by
  simp only [digit, pow_one] at *
  omega

/-! ## The contract, for a `u16` key

Two theorems, one per branch of `n_passes`. They are the whole specification the
extracted code has to meet, and they mention no `Slice`, no `Usize` and no
`Result` -- which is the point of the split.
-/

open real_kernel

/-- The digit the extracted code selects on pass `p`. -/
def symDigit (p : Nat) (s : SymFreq) : Nat := digit p s.key.val

theorem key_lt (s : SymFreq) : s.key.val < 65536 := by scalar_tac

/-- The state after `k` passes: `k` stable passes by digits `0, 1, ...`. -/
def Passed (xs : List SymFreq) : Nat → List SymFreq → Prop
  | 0, ys => ys = xs
  | k + 1, zs => ∃ ys, Passed xs k ys ∧ IsPass (symDigit k) ys zs

theorem Passed.perm {xs ys : List SymFreq} {k : Nat} (h : Passed xs k ys) :
    ys.Perm xs := by
  induction k generalizing ys with
  | zero => rw [Passed] at h; exact h ▸ List.Perm.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    obtain ⟨zs, hzs, hpass⟩ := h
    exact (hpass.perm (fun s _ => digit_lt _ _)).trans (ih hzs)

/-- A histogram computed once, at the start, is still right for the later passes:
`countP` does not care about order, and every pass is a permutation. This is the
fact that makes `radix_sort_symbols` legal at all, and it is easy to miss. -/
theorem total_of_perm (d : SymFreq → Nat) {ys xs : List SymFreq} (h : ys.Perm xs)
    (b : Nat) : total d ys b = total d xs b := h.countP_eq _

theorem start_of_perm (d : SymFreq → Nat) {ys xs : List SymFreq} (h : ys.Perm xs)
    (b : Nat) : start d ys b = start d xs b := by
  simp only [start]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun c _ => total_of_perm d h c)

/-- The `n_passes = 1` test: if every element counted into bucket 0, every
element's digit *is* 0. -/
theorem all_digit_zero (d : SymFreq → Nat) (xs : List SymFreq)
    (h : total d xs 0 = xs.length) : ∀ s ∈ xs, d s = 0 := by
  intro s hs
  have := List.countP_eq_length.mp h s hs
  simpa using this

/-- One pass suffices when every key fits in its low byte -- the `n_passes = 1`
shortcut the Rust takes when `hist[1][0] == symbols0.len()`. -/
theorem sorted_of_one_pass {xs ys : List SymFreq}
    (h1 : IsPass (symDigit 0) xs ys) (hhigh : ∀ s ∈ xs, symDigit 1 s = 0) :
    ys.Perm xs ∧ ys.Pairwise (fun a b => a.key.val ≤ b.key.val) := by
  have hd0 : ∀ s ∈ xs, symDigit 0 s < R := fun s _ => digit_lt 0 _
  refine ⟨h1.perm hd0, ?_⟩
  simp only [symDigit] at hhigh
  rw [List.pairwise_iff_getElem]
  intro i j hi hj hij
  obtain ⟨j1, j2, hj1, hj2, e1, e2, hcase⟩ := h1.mono hd0 hi hj hij
  rw [e1, e2]
  refine le_of_digit_eq (key_lt _) (key_lt _) ?_ ?_
  · rw [hhigh _ (List.getElem_mem hj1), hhigh _ (List.getElem_mem hj2)]
  · simp only [symDigit] at hcase
    rcases hcase with hc | ⟨hc, _⟩ <;> omega

/-- Two passes sort by the whole key. The second pass is stable, so within a
high-byte bucket the first pass's low-byte order survives -- which is the only
reason least-significant-digit radix sort is correct. -/
theorem sorted_of_two_passes {xs ys zs : List SymFreq}
    (h1 : IsPass (symDigit 0) xs ys) (h2 : IsPass (symDigit 1) ys zs) :
    zs.Perm xs ∧ zs.Pairwise (fun a b => a.key.val ≤ b.key.val) := by
  have hd0 : ∀ s ∈ xs, symDigit 0 s < R := fun s _ => digit_lt 0 _
  have hd1 : ∀ s ∈ ys, symDigit 1 s < R := fun s _ => digit_lt 1 _
  refine ⟨(h2.perm hd1).trans (h1.perm hd0), ?_⟩
  have hys : ys.Pairwise (fun a b => symDigit 0 a ≤ symDigit 0 b) := h1.sorted hd0
  rw [List.pairwise_iff_getElem]
  intro i j hi hj hij
  obtain ⟨j1, j2, hj1, hj2, e1, e2, hcase⟩ := h2.mono hd1 hi hj hij
  rw [e1, e2]
  rcases hcase with hc | ⟨hc, hlt⟩
  · exact le_of_digit_lt (key_lt _) (key_lt _) (by simpa [symDigit] using hc)
  · refine le_of_digit_eq (key_lt _) (key_lt _) (by simpa [symDigit] using hc) ?_
    simpa [symDigit] using List.pairwise_iff_getElem.mp hys j1 j2 hj1 hj2 hlt

end RadixSort
import Sort.Model

/-!
# The extracted Rust meets the contract

This is the other half of the experiment: `Sort/Model.lean` is what a substrate
would prove once, and this file is what a *miner* would have to prove about their
own replacement kernel. The line counts of the two files are the measurement.

Nothing here is clever. It is four loop invariants and a lot of index arithmetic,
which is exactly the point: the question is not whether it can be done but what
it costs.
-/

namespace RadixSort
open Aeneas Aeneas.Std real_kernel

/-! ## Bytes to digits

The Rust selects a digit with `(key >> (8*pass)) & 0xFF`. `digit` in the model is
`k / 256 ^ p % 256`. These two lemmas are the whole bridge.
-/

theorem and255_val (x : Std.U16) : (x &&& 255#u16).val = x.val % 256 := by
  show (Std.UScalar.and x 255#u16).val = _
  simp only [Std.UScalar.and, Std.UScalar.val, BitVec.toNat_and]
  have h255 : (255#u16 : Std.U16).bv.toNat = 2 ^ 8 - 1 := by decide
  rw [h255, Nat.and_two_pow_sub_one_eq_mod]

theorem digit_eq (x z : Std.U16) (p : Nat) (hz : z.val = x.val >>> (8 * p)) :
    (z &&& 255#u16).val = digit p x.val := by
  rw [and255_val, hz, Nat.shiftRight_eq_div_pow, digit, Nat.pow_mul]

/-! ## The histogram arrays

`hv` reads a histogram cell as a `Nat`. `getElem!` rather than a proof-carrying
index keeps the "index is below 256" side condition out of every statement; the
`Array _ 256#usize` type already fixes the length.
-/

def hv (l : List Std.Usize) (b : Nat) : Nat := (l[b]!).val

theorem hv_getElem (l : List Std.Usize) {b : Nat} (h : b < l.length) :
    hv l b = (l[b]).val := by
  rw [hv, getElem!_pos l b h]

theorem hv_set (l : List Std.Usize) (i : Nat) (v : Std.Usize) {b : Nat}
    (hi : i < l.length) :
    hv (l.set i v) b = if b = i then v.val else hv l b := by
  rcases eq_or_ne b i with h | h
  · subst h; simp [hv, getElem!_pos, hi]
  · simp [hv, h]

/-- The low byte of the key is the model's digit 0.

Stated over the `.val` equation `step*` actually produces -- `i1.val = (key &&& 255).val`,
not `i1 = key &&& 255` -- so that it applies without massaging. -/
theorem cast_and255 {y x : Std.U16} (h : y.val = (x &&& 255#u16).val) :
    (Std.UScalar.cast .Usize y).val = digit 0 x.val := by
  rw [Std.U16.cast_Usize_val_eq, h, and255_val, digit]
  norm_num

/-- The high byte, via the `>> 8` the Rust does first. -/
theorem cast_and255_shift {z y x : Std.U16} (hz : z.val = (y &&& 255#u16).val)
    (hy : y.val = x.val >>> 8) :
    (Std.UScalar.cast .Usize z).val = digit 1 x.val := by
  rw [Std.U16.cast_Usize_val_eq, hz, and255_val, hy, Nat.shiftRight_eq_div_pow, digit]
  norm_num

/-! ## Loop 0: the histogram

The invariant is `hist_p[b] = cnt p b i`: each cell counts the elements seen so
far. `step*` discharges the plumbing and leaves the six side conditions -- two
index bounds, two `usize` overflow checks, and the same two bounds again for the
writes -- plus the invariant step and the exit.
-/

theorem loop0_spec (xs : Slice SymFreq) (n : Std.Usize) (hn : n.val = xs.length)
    (a0 a1 : Array Std.Usize 256#usize) (i : Std.Usize) (hi : i.val ≤ xs.length)
    (h0 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a0.val b = cnt (symDigit 0) xs.val b i.val)
    (h1 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a1.val b = cnt (symDigit 1) xs.val b i.val) :
    radix_sort_indexed_loop0 xs n a0 a1 i ⦃ r =>
      (∀ b, b < 256 → hv r.1.val b = total (symDigit 0) xs.val b) ∧
      (∀ b, b < 256 → hv r.2.val b = total (symDigit 1) xs.val b) ⦄ := by
  rw [radix_sort_indexed_loop0]
  apply Std.loop.spec_decr_nat
    (measure := fun s => xs.length - s.2.2.val)
    (inv := fun s => s.2.2.val ≤ xs.length ∧
      (∀ b, b < 256 → hv s.1.val b = cnt (symDigit 0) xs.val b s.2.2.val) ∧
      (∀ b, b < 256 → hv s.2.1.val b = cnt (symDigit 1) xs.val b s.2.2.val))
  · rintro ⟨b0, b1, j⟩ ⟨hj, hb0, hb1⟩
    dsimp only at hj hb0 hb1
    simp only [radix_sort_indexed_loop0.body]
    have hlen0 : b0.val.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    have hlen1 : b1.val.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    have hlen0' : b0.length = 256 := hlen0
    have hlen1' : b1.length = 256 := hlen1
    have hmax : xs.length ≤ Std.Usize.max := Std.Slice.length_ineq xs
    step*
    -- the low-byte index is a masked byte, so below 256
    · have h2 : i2.val = digit 0 sf.key.val := by rw [i2_post]; exact cast_and255 i1_post1
      have := digit_lt 0 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    -- the count of a bucket is at most the number of elements seen, so no overflow
    · have hlt : j.val < xs.length := by scalar_tac
      have h2 : i2.val = digit 0 sf.key.val := by rw [i2_post]; exact cast_and255 i1_post1
      have hd := digit_lt 0 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at hd
      have hv3 : i3.val = cnt (symDigit 0) xs.val i2.val j.val := by
        rw [i3_post, ← hv_getElem b0.val (by omega), hb0 _ (by omega)]
      have := cnt_le_index (symDigit 0) xs.val i2.val j.val
      scalar_tac
    · have h2 : i2.val = digit 0 sf.key.val := by rw [i2_post]; exact cast_and255 i1_post1
      have := digit_lt 0 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    · have h7 : i7.val = digit 1 sf.key.val := by
        rw [i7_post]; exact cast_and255_shift i6_post1 i5_post1
      have := digit_lt 1 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    · have hlt : j.val < xs.length := by scalar_tac
      have h7 : i7.val = digit 1 sf.key.val := by
        rw [i7_post]; exact cast_and255_shift i6_post1 i5_post1
      have hd := digit_lt 1 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at hd
      have hv8 : i8.val = cnt (symDigit 1) xs.val i7.val j.val := by
        rw [i8_post, ← hv_getElem b1.val (by omega), hb1 _ (by omega)]
      have := cnt_le_index (symDigit 1) xs.val i7.val j.val
      scalar_tac
    · have h7 : i7.val = digit 1 sf.key.val := by
        rw [i7_post]; exact cast_and255_shift i6_post1 i5_post1
      have := digit_lt 1 sf.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    -- the invariant step: one more element counted in one bucket of each histogram
    · have hlt : j.val < xs.length := by scalar_tac
      have hd0 : i2.val = symDigit 0 xs.val[j.val] := by
        rw [i2_post, cast_and255 i1_post1, sf_post, symDigit]
      have hd1 : i7.val = symDigit 1 xs.val[j.val] := by
        rw [i7_post, cast_and255_shift i6_post1 i5_post1, sf_post, symDigit]
      refine ⟨by omega, ?_, ?_, by omega⟩
      · intro b hb
        have h2 : i2.val < 256 := by
          have := digit_lt 0 (xs.val[j.val]).key.val
          simp only [R] at this
          rw [hd0, symDigit]
          omega
        rw [a_post, Std.Array.set_val_eq, hv_set b0.val _ _ (by omega), i10_post,
          cnt_succ _ _ _ _ hlt, ← hd0]
        rcases eq_or_ne b i2.val with h | h
        · subst h
          rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl, i4_post, i3_post,
            ← hv_getElem b0.val (by omega), hb0 _ (by omega)]
        · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (Ne.symm h), hb0 _ hb]
          omega
      · intro b hb
        have h7 : i7.val < 256 := by
          have := digit_lt 1 (xs.val[j.val]).key.val
          simp only [R] at this
          rw [hd1, symDigit]
          omega
        rw [a1_post, Std.Array.set_val_eq, hv_set b1.val _ _ (by omega), i10_post,
          cnt_succ _ _ _ _ hlt, ← hd1]
        rcases eq_or_ne b i7.val with h | h
        · subst h
          rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl, i9_post, i8_post,
            ← hv_getElem b1.val (by omega), hb1 _ (by omega)]
        · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (Ne.symm h), hb1 _ hb]
          omega
    -- the exit: `i` has reached the end, so every count is a total
    · have hge : xs.length ≤ j.val := by scalar_tac
      exact ⟨fun b hb => by rw [hb0 b hb, cnt_of_length_le _ _ _ hge],
             fun b hb => by rw [hb1 b hb, cnt_of_length_le _ _ _ hge]⟩
  · exact ⟨hi, h0, h1⟩

/-! ## Loop 1a: the prefix sums

`offsets[b]` becomes the start of bucket `b`, and `offset` runs ahead of it as the
running total. The `if pass = 0` inside the body picks which histogram to read, so
`step*` splits and each half is discharged against the matching hypothesis.
-/

theorem loop1_loop0_spec (xs : Slice SymFreq) (a0 a1 : Array Std.Usize 256#usize)
    (p : Std.Usize) (hp : p.val < 2)
    (h0 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a0.val b = total (symDigit 0) xs.val b)
    (h1 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a1.val b = total (symDigit 1) xs.val b)
    (offs : Array Std.Usize 256#usize) (offset k : Std.Usize)
    (hk : k.val ≤ 256)
    (hoffset : offset.val = start (symDigit p.val) xs.val k.val)
    (hinv : ∀ b, b < k.val → hv offs.val b = start (symDigit p.val) xs.val b) :
    radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop0 a0 a1 p offs offset k ⦃ r =>
      ∀ b, b < 256 → hv r.val b = start (symDigit p.val) xs.val b ⦄ := by
  rw [radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop0]
  apply Std.loop.spec_decr_nat
    (measure := fun s => 256 - s.2.2.val)
    (inv := fun s => s.2.2.val ≤ 256 ∧
      s.2.1.val = start (symDigit p.val) xs.val s.2.2.val ∧
      (∀ b, b < s.2.2.val → hv s.1.val b = start (symDigit p.val) xs.val b))
  · rintro ⟨os, off, k'⟩ ⟨hk', hoff, hos⟩
    dsimp only at hk' hoff hos
    simp only [radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop0.body]
    have hlenos : os.val.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    have hlenos' : os.length = 256 := hlenos
    have hlen0 : a0.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    have hlen1 : a1.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    -- the sum of all the buckets is the number of elements, so no offset overflows
    have hsum : start (symDigit p.val) xs.val 256 = xs.length :=
      start_R _ _ (fun s _ => digit_lt _ _)
    have hmax : xs.length ≤ Std.Usize.max := Std.Slice.length_ineq xs
    -- Pull the `if` out of the read so the two passes share one proof: which
    -- histogram is read is a choice of array, not a choice of program.
    have hite : (if p = 0#usize then Std.Array.index_usize a0 k'
        else Std.Array.index_usize a1 k')
        = Std.Array.index_usize (if p = 0#usize then a0 else a1) k' := by
      split <;> rfl
    rw [hite]
    have hlenA : (if p = 0#usize then a0 else a1).length = 256 := by
      split
      · exact hlen0
      · exact hlen1
    have hA : ∀ b, b < 256 →
        hv (if p = 0#usize then a0 else a1).val b = total (symDigit p.val) xs.val b := by
      split
      · rename_i h; rw [h]; exact h0
      · rename_i h
        have hp1 : p.val = 1 := by scalar_tac
        rw [hp1]; exact h1
    have hlenA' : (if p = 0#usize then a0 else a1).val.length = 256 := hlenA
    step*
    -- no offset overflows, because the last one is the number of elements
    · have hk'' : k'.val < 256 := by scalar_tac
      have hi : i.val = total (symDigit p.val) xs.val k'.val := by
        rw [i_post, ← hv_getElem _ (by omega), hA _ hk'']
      have hstep := start_succ (symDigit p.val) xs.val k'.val
      have hle : start (symDigit p.val) xs.val (k'.val + 1)
          ≤ start (symDigit p.val) xs.val 256 := start_mono _ _ (by omega)
      rw [hsum] at hle
      omega
    -- the invariant step: one more bucket start recorded, offset moved past it
    · have hk'' : k'.val < 256 := by scalar_tac
      have hi : i.val = total (symDigit p.val) xs.val k'.val := by
        rw [i_post, ← hv_getElem _ (by omega), hA _ hk'']
      refine ⟨by omega, ?_, ?_, by omega⟩
      · rw [k1_post, offset1_post, hoff, hi, start_succ]
      · intro b hb
        rw [a_post, Std.Array.set_val_eq, hv_set os.val _ _ (by omega)]
        rcases eq_or_ne b k'.val with h | h
        · subst h; rw [if_pos rfl, hoff]
        · rw [if_neg h]
          rw [k1_post] at hb
          exact hos b (by omega)
  · exact ⟨hk, hoffset, hinv⟩

/-! ## Loop 1b: the scatter

The one that matters. `in1` says which buffer is the source this pass; both are
threaded through the loop state, and only the destination is written. Two `if in1`
branches appear in the body, and both are pulled out into a *choice of slice*
before `step*` runs, so the proof is not written twice.

The invariant is `IsPass` restricted to the elements seen so far, plus
`offsets[b] = posAt b j` -- the cursor of bucket `b` is where its next element goes.
-/

/-- The buffer this pass reads. -/
@[reducible] def rd (in1 : Bool) (a b : Slice SymFreq) : Slice SymFreq := if in1 then b else a

/-- The buffer this pass writes. -/
@[reducible] def wr (in1 : Bool) (a b : Slice SymFreq) : Slice SymFreq := if in1 then a else b

/-- The high byte with the shift amount the Rust computes, `pass * 8`. -/
theorem cast_and255_shiftp {z y x : Std.U16} {q : Nat} (hz : z.val = (y &&& 255#u16).val)
    (hy : y.val = x.val >>> (q * 8)) :
    (Std.UScalar.cast .Usize z).val = digit q x.val := by
  rw [Std.U16.cast_Usize_val_eq, hz, and255_val, hy, Nat.shiftRight_eq_div_pow, digit,
    Nat.mul_comm q 8, Nat.pow_mul]

/-- The pair the body writes back: the updated slice goes in the slot `in1` picks. -/
@[reducible] def put0 (in1 : Bool) (sa s : Slice SymFreq) : Slice SymFreq :=
  if in1 then s else sa

@[reducible] def put1 (in1 : Bool) (sb s : Slice SymFreq) : Slice SymFreq :=
  if in1 then sb else s

/-- The destination after the write is the updated slice, whichever way `in1` went.
This and `rd_put` are where the two branches get collapsed, once. -/
theorem wr_put (in1 : Bool) (sa sb s : Slice SymFreq) :
    wr in1 (put0 in1 sa s) (put1 in1 sb s) = s := by
  unfold wr put0 put1; split <;> simp

theorem rd_put (in1 : Bool) (sa sb s : Slice SymFreq) :
    rd in1 (put0 in1 sa s) (put1 in1 sb s) = rd in1 sa sb := by
  unfold rd put0 put1; split <;> simp

theorem loop1_loop1_spec (src s0 s1 : Slice SymFreq) (n : Std.Usize) (in1 : Bool)
    (p : Std.Usize) (offs : Array Std.Usize 256#usize) (j : Std.Usize)
    (hp : p.val < 2)
    (hn : n.val = src.length)
    (hsrc : rd in1 s0 s1 = src)
    (hdst : (wr in1 s0 s1).length = src.length)
    (hj : j.val ≤ src.length)
    (hoffs : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv offs.val b = posAt (symDigit p.val) src.val b j.val)
    (hwr : ∀ (t : Nat), t < j.val → ∀ (h : t < src.val.length),
      (wr in1 s0 s1).val[posAt (symDigit p.val) src.val (symDigit p.val src.val[t]) t]?
        = some src.val[t]) :
    radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop1 s0 s1 n in1 p offs j ⦃ r =>
      rd in1 r.1 r.2 = src ∧ IsPass (symDigit p.val) src.val (wr in1 r.1 r.2).val ⦄ := by
  rw [radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop1]
  apply Std.loop.spec_decr_nat
    (measure := fun st => src.length - st.2.2.2.val)
    (inv := fun st => st.2.2.2.val ≤ src.length ∧
      rd in1 st.1 st.2.1 = src ∧
      (wr in1 st.1 st.2.1).length = src.length ∧
      (∀ b, b < 256 → hv st.2.2.1.val b = posAt (symDigit p.val) src.val b st.2.2.2.val) ∧
      (∀ (t : Nat), t < st.2.2.2.val → ∀ (h : t < src.val.length),
        (wr in1 st.1 st.2.1).val[posAt (symDigit p.val) src.val
          (symDigit p.val src.val[t]) t]? = some src.val[t]))
  · rintro ⟨sa, sb, os, j'⟩ ⟨hj', hrd, hlen, hoff, hwrit⟩
    dsimp only at hj' hrd hlen hoff hwrit
    -- The source buffer is never written, so name it by what it is rather than
    -- carrying an equation: this keeps every `getElem` proof term intact, which a
    -- `rw` under `[·]` would break.
    subst hrd
    simp only [radix_sort_indexed_loop1_loop1.body]
    have hite1 : (if in1 = true then Std.Slice.index_usize sb j'
        else Std.Slice.index_usize sa j') = Std.Slice.index_usize (rd in1 sa sb) j' := by
      unfold rd; split <;> rfl
    have hite2 : ∀ (slot : Std.Usize) (sym : SymFreq),
        (if in1 = true then (do let s ← Std.Slice.update sa slot sym; Result.ok (s, sb))
         else (do let s ← Std.Slice.update sb slot sym; Result.ok (sa, s)))
        = (do let s ← Std.Slice.update (wr in1 sa sb) slot sym
              Result.ok (put0 in1 sa s, put1 in1 sb s)) := by
      intro slot sym; unfold wr put0 put1; split <;> simp
    rw [hite1]
    simp only [hite2]
    have hlenos : os.val.length = 256 := by scalar_tac
    have hlenos' : os.length = 256 := hlenos
    have hmaxlen : (rd in1 sa sb).length ≤ Std.Usize.max :=
      Std.Slice.length_ineq (rd in1 sa sb)
    -- `Slice.length` and `.val.length` are the same by definition but are two
    -- different atoms to `omega`, so state the arithmetic facts in one form.
    have hlen' : (wr in1 sa sb).val.length = (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := hlen
    have hn' : n.val = (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := hn
    have hj'' : j'.val ≤ (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := hj'
    have hmaxlen' : (rd in1 sa sb).val.length ≤ Std.Usize.max := hmaxlen
    step*
    -- the digit is a masked byte, so it indexes `offsets`
    · have hd : d.val = digit p.val sym.key.val := by
        rw [d_post]; exact cast_and255_shiftp (x := sym.key) (q := p.val) i2_post1 (by rw [i1_post1, i_post])
      have := digit_lt p.val sym.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    -- the write lands inside the destination, by `posAt_lt`
    · have hlt : j'.val < (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := by scalar_tac
      have hd : d.val = symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val] := by
        rw [d_post, cast_and255_shiftp (x := sym.key) (q := p.val) i2_post1 (by rw [i1_post1, i_post]), sym_post, symDigit]
      have hdb : d.val < 256 := by
        have := digit_lt p.val ((rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]).key.val
        simp only [R] at this
        rw [hd, symDigit]
        omega
      have hslot : slot.val = posAt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val
          (symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]) j'.val := by
        rw [slot_post, ← hv_getElem os.val (by omega), hoff _ hdb, hd]
      have := posAt_lt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val (fun s _ => digit_lt _ _) hlt
      omega
    -- and so the cursor can be advanced without overflow
    · have hlt : j'.val < (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := by scalar_tac
      have hd : d.val = symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val] := by
        rw [d_post, cast_and255_shiftp (x := sym.key) (q := p.val) i2_post1 (by rw [i1_post1, i_post]), sym_post, symDigit]
      have hdb : d.val < 256 := by
        have := digit_lt p.val ((rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]).key.val
        simp only [R] at this
        rw [hd, symDigit]
        omega
      have hslot : slot.val = posAt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val
          (symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]) j'.val := by
        rw [slot_post, ← hv_getElem os.val (by omega), hoff _ hdb, hd]
      have := posAt_lt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val (fun s _ => digit_lt _ _) hlt
      scalar_tac
    · have hd : d.val = digit p.val sym.key.val := by
        rw [d_post]; exact cast_and255_shiftp (x := sym.key) (q := p.val) i2_post1 (by rw [i1_post1, i_post])
      have := digit_lt p.val sym.key.val
      simp only [R] at this
      omega
    -- the invariant step: one element placed, one bucket cursor advanced
    · have hlt : j'.val < (rd in1 sa sb).val.length := by scalar_tac
      have hd : d.val = symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val] := by
        rw [d_post, cast_and255_shiftp (x := sym.key) (q := p.val) i2_post1 (by rw [i1_post1, i_post]), sym_post, symDigit]
      have hdb : d.val < 256 := by
        have := digit_lt p.val ((rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]).key.val
        simp only [R] at this
        rw [hd, symDigit]
        omega
      have hslot : slot.val = posAt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val
          (symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[j'.val]) j'.val := by
        rw [slot_post, ← hv_getElem os.val (by omega), hoff _ hdb, hd]
      have hposlt := posAt_lt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val (fun s _ => digit_lt _ _) hlt
      have hslotlt : slot.val < (wr in1 sa sb).val.length := by
        rw [hslot]; omega
      refine ⟨by omega, rd_put in1 sa sb x, ?_, ?_, ?_, by omega⟩
      · rw [wr_put, x_post]
        simp only [Std.Slice.set_val_eq, Std.Slice.length, List.length_set]
        exact hlen
      · intro b hb
        rw [a_post, Std.Array.set_val_eq, hv_set os.val _ _ (by omega), j1_post, posAt,
          cnt_succ _ _ _ _ hlt, ← hd]
        rcases eq_or_ne b d.val with h | h
        · subst h
          rw [if_pos rfl, if_pos rfl, i3_post, hslot, hd, posAt]
          omega
        · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (Ne.symm h), hoff b hb, posAt]
          omega
      · intro t ht h
        rw [wr_put, x_post, Std.Slice.set_val_eq]
        rw [j1_post] at ht
        rcases eq_or_ne t j'.val with hc | hc
        · subst hc
          rw [← hslot, List.getElem?_set_self hslotlt, sym_post]
        · have hne : posAt (symDigit p.val) (rd in1 sa sb).val
              (symDigit p.val (rd in1 sa sb).val[t]) t ≠ slot.val := by
            rw [hslot]
            exact posAt_ne _ _ h hlt hc
          rw [List.getElem?_set_ne (Ne.symm hne)]
          exact hwrit t (by omega) h
    -- the exit: every element has been placed, which is exactly `IsPass`
    · have hge : (rd in1 sa sb).length ≤ j'.val := by scalar_tac
      have hge' : (rd in1 sa sb).val.length ≤ j'.val := hge
      exact ⟨hlen, fun t h => hwrit t (by omega) h⟩
  · exact ⟨hj, hsrc, hdst, hoffs, hwr⟩

/-! ## Loop 1: the passes

The outer loop flips `in1` and advances `pass`. Its invariant is `Passed`: the
buffer `in1` currently designates holds the input after `pass` stable passes.
-/

theorem rd_not (in1 : Bool) (a b : Slice SymFreq) : rd (!in1) a b = wr in1 a b := by
  unfold rd wr; cases in1 <;> simp

theorem wr_not (in1 : Bool) (a b : Slice SymFreq) : wr (!in1) a b = rd in1 a b := by
  unfold rd wr; cases in1 <;> simp

theorem loop1_spec (xs : Slice SymFreq) (n : Std.Usize) (hn : n.val = xs.length)
    (a0 a1 : Array Std.Usize 256#usize) (np : Std.Usize) (hnp : np.val ≤ 2)
    (h0 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a0.val b = total (symDigit 0) xs.val b)
    (h1 : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a1.val b = total (symDigit 1) xs.val b)
    (s0 s1 : Slice SymFreq) (in1 : Bool) (pass : Std.Usize)
    (hpass : pass.val ≤ np.val)
    (hsrclen : (rd in1 s0 s1).length = xs.length)
    (hdstlen : (wr in1 s0 s1).length = xs.length)
    (hpassed : Passed xs.val pass.val (rd in1 s0 s1).val) :
    radix_sort_indexed_loop1 s0 s1 n a0 a1 np in1 pass ⦃ r =>
      Passed xs.val np.val (rd r.1 r.2.1 r.2.2).val ⦄ := by
  rw [radix_sort_indexed_loop1]
  apply Std.loop.spec_decr_nat
    (measure := fun st => np.val - st.2.2.2.val)
    (inv := fun st => st.2.2.2.val ≤ np.val ∧
      (rd st.2.2.1 st.1 st.2.1).length = xs.length ∧
      (wr st.2.2.1 st.1 st.2.1).length = xs.length ∧
      Passed xs.val st.2.2.2.val (rd st.2.2.1 st.1 st.2.1).val)
  · rintro ⟨sa, sb, flag, pass'⟩ ⟨hp', hsl, hdl, hpd⟩
    dsimp only at hp' hsl hdl hpd
    simp only [radix_sort_indexed_loop1.body]
    split
    case isTrue hlt =>
      have hltv : pass'.val < np.val := by scalar_tac
      have hperm : (rd flag sa sb).val.Perm xs.val := hpd.perm
      have h0' : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a0.val b = total (symDigit 0) (rd flag sa sb).val b := by
        intro b hb; rw [h0 b hb, total_of_perm _ hperm]
      have h1' : ∀ b, b < 256 → hv a1.val b = total (symDigit 1) (rd flag sa sb).val b := by
        intro b hb; rw [h1 b hb, total_of_perm _ hperm]
      have hz : (0#usize : Std.Usize).val = 0 := by scalar_tac
      apply Std.WP.spec_bind (loop1_loop0_spec (rd flag sa sb) a0 a1 pass' (by omega) h0' h1'
        (Std.Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize) 0#usize 0#usize (by scalar_tac)
        (by rw [hz, start]; simp)
        (by intro b hb; exact absurd hb (by scalar_tac)))
      intro offs1 hoffs1
      apply Std.WP.spec_bind (loop1_loop1_spec (rd flag sa sb) sa sb n flag pass' offs1 0#usize
        (by omega) (by rw [hn, ← hsl]) rfl (by rw [hdl, hsl]) (by scalar_tac)
        (by intro b hb; rw [hoffs1 b hb, posAt, hz, cnt_zero]; omega)
        (by intro t ht; exact absurd ht (by scalar_tac)))
      rintro ⟨sa', sb'⟩ ⟨hrd', hpass'⟩
      apply Std.WP.spec_bind (Std.Usize.add_spec (y := 1#usize) (by scalar_tac))
      intro pass1 hp1
      have hp1' : pass1.val = pass'.val + 1 := by simpa using hp1
      -- the extracted `¬ in1` is `decide (¬ in1 = true)`; normalise it to `!in1`
      have hnot : (decide (¬ flag = true)) = !flag := by cases flag <;> simp
      simp only [Std.WP.spec_ok, hnot]
      refine ⟨⟨by omega, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, by omega⟩
      · rw [rd_not]; exact hpass'.1.trans hsl
      · rw [wr_not, hrd']; exact hsl
      · rw [rd_not, hp1']
        exact ⟨(rd flag sa sb).val, hpd, hpass'⟩
    case isFalse hge =>
      have : pass'.val = np.val := by scalar_tac
      rw [← this]
      exact hpd
  · exact ⟨hpass, hsrclen, hdstlen, hpassed⟩

/-! ## The theorem

`radix_sort_indexed` returns a flag saying which buffer holds the answer. The
theorem is about that buffer: it is a permutation of the input, ordered by key.
-/

theorem radix_sort_indexed_spec (s0 s1 : Slice SymFreq) (hlen : s1.length = s0.length) :
    radix_sort_indexed s0 s1 ⦃ r =>
      (rd r.1 r.2.1 r.2.2).val.Perm s0.val ∧
      (rd r.1 r.2.1 r.2.2).val.Pairwise (fun a b => a.key.val ≤ b.key.val) ⦄ := by
  rw [radix_sort_indexed]
  have hz : (0#usize : Std.Usize).val = 0 := by scalar_tac
  have hrep : ∀ b, b < 256 →
      hv (Std.Array.repeat 256#usize (0#usize : Std.Usize)).val b = 0 := by
    intro b hb
    rw [hv, Std.Array.repeat_val,
      getElem!_pos _ b (by rw [List.length_replicate]; scalar_tac), List.getElem_replicate]
    scalar_tac
  have hn : (Std.Slice.len s0).val = s0.val.length := Std.Slice.len_val s0
  apply Std.WP.spec_bind (loop0_spec s0 (Std.Slice.len s0) hn
    (Std.Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize) (Std.Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize) 0#usize
    (by scalar_tac)
    (by intro b hb; rw [hrep b hb, hz, cnt_zero])
    (by intro b hb; rw [hrep b hb, hz, cnt_zero]))
  rintro ⟨c0, c1⟩ ⟨hc0, hc1⟩
  dsimp only at hc0 hc1
  apply Std.WP.spec_bind (Std.Array.index_usize_spec c1 0#usize (by scalar_tac))
  intro i hi
  have hival : i.val = total (symDigit 1) s0.val 0 := by
    rw [hi, ← hv_getElem c1.val (by scalar_tac), hz, hc1 0 (by omega)]
  -- `rd false s0 s1` is `s0`, and `wr false s0 s1` is `s1`
  have hrd0 : rd false s0 s1 = s0 := by unfold rd; simp
  have hwr0 : wr false s0 s1 = s1 := by unfold wr; simp
  split
  -- one pass: every key's high byte is zero, so the low-byte pass sorts by key
  case isTrue heq =>
    have htot : total (symDigit 1) s0.val 0 = s0.val.length := by
      rw [← hival, ← hn, heq]
    have hhigh : ∀ s ∈ s0.val, symDigit 1 s = 0 := all_digit_zero _ _ htot
    refine Std.WP.spec_mono' (loop1_spec s0 (Std.Slice.len s0) hn c0 c1 1#usize
      (by scalar_tac) hc0 hc1 s0 s1 false 0#usize (by scalar_tac)
      (by rw [hrd0]) (by rw [hwr0]; exact hlen)
      (by rw [hz, Passed, hrd0])) ?_
    intro r hr
    have hnp : (1#usize : Std.Usize).val = 1 := by scalar_tac
    rw [hnp, Passed] at hr
    obtain ⟨ys, hys, hpass⟩ := hr
    rw [Passed] at hys
    subst hys
    exact sorted_of_one_pass hpass hhigh
  -- two passes
  case isFalse hne =>
    refine Std.WP.spec_mono' (loop1_spec s0 (Std.Slice.len s0) hn c0 c1 2#usize
      (by scalar_tac) hc0 hc1 s0 s1 false 0#usize (by scalar_tac)
      (by rw [hrd0]) (by rw [hwr0]; exact hlen)
      (by rw [hz, Passed, hrd0])) ?_
    intro r hr
    have hnp : (2#usize : Std.Usize).val = 2 := by scalar_tac
    rw [hnp, Passed] at hr
    obtain ⟨ys, hys, hpass1⟩ := hr
    rw [Passed] at hys
    obtain ⟨zs, hzs, hpass0⟩ := hys
    rw [Passed] at hzs
    subst hzs
    exact sorted_of_two_passes hpass0 hpass1

end RadixSortimport Sort.Model

  (n : Std.Usize) (in1 : Bool) (pass : Std.Usize)
  (symbols0 : Slice indexed.SymFreq) (symbols1 : Slice indexed.SymFreq)
  (offsets : Array Std.Usize 256#usize) (j : Std.Usize) :

/-- [real_kernel::original::radix_sort_symbols]:
    Source: 'src/original.rs', lines 10:0-47:1
    Visibility: public -/
def original.radix_sort_symbols
  (symbols0 : Slice indexed.SymFreq) (symbols1 : Slice indexed.SymFreq) :
  Result ((Slice indexed.SymFreq) × (Slice indexed.SymFreq → ((Slice
    indexed.SymFreq) × (Slice indexed.SymFreq))))
  := do
  let a := Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize
  let hist := Array.repeat 2#usize a
  let iter ← core.slice.Slice.iter symbols0
  let hist1 ← original.radix_sort_symbols_loop0 iter hist
  let i := Slice.len symbols0
  let a1 ← Array.index_usize hist1 1#usize
  let i1 ← Array.index_usize a1 0#usize
  let n_passes ← if i = i1
                   then 2#usize - 1#usize
                   else ok 2#usize
  let s ← lift (Array.to_slice hist1)
  let i2 ← core.slice.Slice.iter s
  let e ←
    core.iter.traits.iterator.Iterator.enumerate.trait_default
      (core.iter.traits.iterator.IteratorSliceIter (Array Std.Usize 256#usize))
      i2
  let iter1 ←
    core.iter.traits.iterator.Iterator.take.trait_default
      (core.iter.traits.iterator.IteratorEnumerate
      (core.iter.traits.iterator.IteratorSliceIter (Array Std.Usize
      256#usize))) e n_passes
  let (current_symbols, new_symbols, back) ←
    original.radix_sort_symbols_loop1 iter1 (fun s1 s2 => (s1, s2)) symbols0
      symbols1
  let back1 := fun s1 => back s1 new_symbols
  ok (current_symbols, back1)

    256#usize) × Std.Usize) ((Array Std.Usize 256#usize) × (Array Std.Usize
    256#usize)))
  := do
  if i < n
  then
    let sf ← Slice.index_usize symbols0 i
    let i1 ← lift (sf.key &&& 255#u16)
    let i2 ← lift (UScalar.cast .Usize i1)
    let i3 ← Array.index_usize hist0 i2
    let i4 ← i3 + 1#usize
    let a ← Array.update hist0 i2 i4
    let i5 ← sf.key >>> 8#i32
    let i6 ← lift (i5 &&& 255#u16)
    let i7 ← lift (UScalar.cast .Usize i6)
    let i8 ← Array.index_usize hist1 i7
    let i9 ← i8 + 1#usize
    let a1 ← Array.update hist1 i7 i9
    let i10 ← i + 1#usize
    ok (cont (a, a1, i10))
  else ok (done (hist0, hist1))

def radix_sort_indexed
  (symbols0 : Slice SymFreq) (symbols1 : Slice SymFreq) :
  Result (Bool × (Slice SymFreq) × (Slice SymFreq))
  := do
  let n := Slice.len symbols0
  let hist0 := Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize
  let hist1 := Array.repeat 256#usize 0#usize
  let (hist01, hist11) ←
    radix_sort_indexed_loop0 symbols0 n hist0 hist1 0#usize
  let i ← Array.index_usize hist11 0#usize
  let n_passes ← if n = i
                   then ok 1#usize
                   else ok 2#usize
  radix_sort_indexed_loop1 symbols0 symbols1 n hist01 hist11 n_passes false
    0#usize

/--
The expression `binderNameHint v binder e` defined to be `e`.

If it is used on the right-hand side of an equation that is used for rewriting by `rw` or `simp`,
and `v` is a local variable, and `binder` is an expression that (after beta-reduction) is a binder
(`fun w => …` or `∀ w, …`), then it will rename `v` to the name used in that binder, and remove
the `binderNameHint`.

A typical use of this gadget would be as follows; the gadget ensures that after rewriting, the local
variable is still `name`, and not `x`:
```
theorem all_eq_not_any_not (l : List α) (p : α → Bool) :
    l.all p = !l.any fun x => binderNameHint x p (!p x) := sorry

example (names : List String) : names.all (fun name => "Waldo".isPrefixOf name) = true := by
  rw [all_eq_not_any_not]
  -- ⊢ (!names.any fun name => !"Waldo".isPrefixOf name) = true
```

If `binder` is not a binder, then the name of `v` attains a macro scope. This only matters when the
resulting term is used in a non-hygienic way, e.g. in termination proofs for well-founded recursion.

This gadget is supported by
* `simp`, `dsimp` and `rw` in the right-hand-side of an equation
* `simp` in the assumptions of congruence rules

It is ineffective in other positions (hypotheses of rewrite rules) or when used by other tactics
(e.g. `apply`).
-/
@[simp ↓, expose]
def binderNameHint {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {γ : Sort w} (v : α) (binder : β) (e : γ) : γ := e

/--
The syntax category of binder predicates contains predicates like `> 0`, `∈ s`, etc.
(`: t` should not be a binder predicate because it would clash with the built-in syntax for ∀/∃.)
-/
declare_syntax_cat binderPred

/--
`satisfies_binder_pred% t pred` expands to a proposition expressing that `t` satisfies `pred`.
-/
syntax "satisfies_binder_pred% " term:max binderPred : term

-- Extend ∀ and ∃ to binder predicates.

/--
The notation `∃ x < 2, p x` is shorthand for `∃ x, x < 2 ∧ p x`,
and similarly for other binary operators.
-/
syntax "∃ " binderIdent binderPred ", " term : term
/--
The notation `∀ x < 2, p x` is shorthand for `∀ x, x < 2 → p x`,
and similarly for other binary operators.
-/
syntax "∀ " binderIdent binderPred ", " term : term

macro_rules
  | `(∃ $x:ident $pred:binderPred, $p) =>
    `(∃ $x:ident, satisfies_binder_pred% $x $pred ∧ $p)
  | `(∃ _ $pred:binderPred, $p) =>
    `(∃ x, satisfies_binder_pred% x $pred ∧ $p)

macro_rules
  | `(∀ $x:ident $pred:binderPred, $p) =>
    `(∀ $x:ident, satisfies_binder_pred% $x $pred → $p)
  | `(∀ _ $pred:binderPred, $p) =>
    `(∀ x, satisfies_binder_pred% x $pred → $p)

/-- Declare `∃ x > y, ...` as syntax for `∃ x, x > y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " > " y:term => `($x > $y)
/-- Declare `∃ x ≥ y, ...` as syntax for `∃ x, x ≥ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ≥ " y:term => `($x ≥ $y)
/-- Declare `∃ x < y, ...` as syntax for `∃ x, x < y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " < " y:term => `($x < $y)
/-- Declare `∃ x ≤ y, ...` as syntax for `∃ x, x ≤ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ≤ " y:term => `($x ≤ $y)
/-- Declare `∃ x ≠ y, ...` as syntax for `∃ x, x ≠ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ≠ " y:term => `($x ≠ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ∈ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ∈ y → ...` and `∃ x ∈ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ∈ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ∈ " y:term => `($x ∈ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ∉ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ∉ y → ...` and `∃ x ∉ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ∉ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ∉ " y:term => `($x ∉ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ⊆ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ⊆ y → ...` and `∃ x ⊆ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ⊆ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ⊆ " y:term => `($x ⊆ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ⊂ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ⊂ y → ...` and `∃ x ⊂ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ⊂ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ⊂ " y:term => `($x ⊂ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ⊇ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ⊇ y → ...` and `∃ x ⊇ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ⊇ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ⊇ " y:term => `($x ⊇ $y)

/-- Declare `∀ x ⊃ y, ...` as syntax for `∀ x, x ⊃ y → ...` and `∃ x ⊃ y, ...` as syntax for
`∃ x, x ⊃ y ∧ ...` -/
binder_predicate x " ⊃ " y:term => `($x ⊃ $y)

/-! # by_cases tactic and if-then-else support -/

/--
`by_cases (h :)? p` splits the main goal into two cases, assuming `h : p` in the first branch, and `h : ¬ p` in the second branch.
-/
syntax "by_cases " (atomic(ident " : "))? term : tactic

macro_rules
  | `(tactic| by_cases $e) => `(tactic| by_cases h : $e)
macro_rules
  | `(tactic| by_cases $h : $e) =>
    `(tactic| open Classical in refine if $h:ident : $e then ?pos else ?neg)

/-! ## if-then-else -/

@[simp] theorem if_true {_ : Decidable True} (t e : α) : ite True t e = t := if_pos trivial

@[simp] theorem if_false {_ : Decidable False} (t e : α) : ite False t e = e := if_neg id

theorem ite_id [Decidable c] {α} (t : α) : (if c then t else t) = t := by split <;> rfl

/-- A function applied to a `dite` is a `dite` of that function applied to each of the branches. -/
theorem apply_dite (f : α → β) (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (x : P → α) (y : ¬P → α) :
    f (dite P x y) = dite P (fun h => f (x h)) (fun h => f (y h)) := by
  by_cases h : P <;> simp [h]

/-- A function applied to a `ite` is a `ite` of that function applied to each of the branches. -/
theorem apply_ite (f : α → β) (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (x y : α) :
    f (ite P x y) = ite P (f x) (f y) :=
  apply_dite f P (fun _ => x) (fun _ => y)

/-- A `dite` whose results do not actually depend on the condition may be reduced to an `ite`. -/
@[simp] theorem dite_eq_ite [Decidable P] :
  (dite P (fun _ => a) (fun _ => b)) = ite P a b := rfl

-- Remark: dite and ite are "defally equal" when we ignore the proofs.
@[deprecated dite_eq_ite (since := "2025-10-29")]
theorem dif_eq_if (c : Prop) {h : Decidable c} {α : Sort u} (t : α) (e : α) : dite c (fun _ => t) (fun _ => e) = ite c t e :=
  match h with
  | isTrue _    => rfl
  | isFalse _   => rfl

module

prelude
public import Init.PropLemmas

@[expose] public section

universe u v

/-! # Classical reasoning support -/

namespace Classical

noncomputable def indefiniteDescription {α : Sort u} (p : α → Prop) (h : ∃ x, p x) : {x // p x} :=
  choice <| let ⟨x, px⟩ := h; ⟨⟨x, px⟩⟩

/--
Given that there exists an element satisfying `p`, returns one such element.

This is a straightforward consequence of, and equivalent to, `Classical.choice`.

See also `choose_spec`, which asserts that the returned value has property `p`.
-/
noncomputable def choose {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : α :=
  (indefiniteDescription p h).val

theorem choose_spec {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : p (choose h) :=
  (indefiniteDescription p h).property

/-- **Diaconescu's theorem**: excluded middle from choice, Function extensionality and propositional extensionality. -/
theorem em (p : Prop) : p ∨ ¬p :=
  let U (x : Prop) : Prop := x = True ∨ p
  let V (x : Prop) : Prop := x = False ∨ p
  have exU : ∃ x, U x := ⟨True, Or.inl rfl⟩
  have exV : ∃ x, V x := ⟨False, Or.inl rfl⟩
  let u : Prop := choose exU
  let v : Prop := choose exV
  have u_def : U u := choose_spec exU
  have v_def : V v := choose_spec exV
  have not_uv_or_p : u ≠ v ∨ p :=
    match u_def, v_def with
    | Or.inr h, _ => Or.inr h
    | _, Or.inr h => Or.inr h
    | Or.inl hut, Or.inl hvf =>
      have hne : u ≠ v := by simp [hvf, hut]
      Or.inl hne
  have p_implies_uv : p → u = v :=
    fun hp =>
    have hpred : U = V :=
      funext fun x =>
        have hl : (x = True ∨ p) → (x = False ∨ p) :=
          fun _ => Or.inr hp
        have hr : (x = False ∨ p) → (x = True ∨ p) :=
          fun _ => Or.inr hp
        show (x = True ∨ p) = (x = False ∨ p) from
          propext (Iff.intro hl hr)
    have h₀ : ∀ exU exV, @choose _ U exU = @choose _ V exV := by
      rw [hpred]; intros; rfl
    show u = v from h₀ _ _
  match not_uv_or_p with
  | Or.inl hne => Or.inr (mt p_implies_uv hne)
  | Or.inr h   => Or.inl h

theorem exists_true_of_nonempty {α : Sort u} : Nonempty α → ∃ _ : α, True
  | ⟨x⟩ => ⟨x, trivial⟩

noncomputable def inhabited_of_nonempty {α : Sort u} (h : Nonempty α) : Inhabited α :=
  ⟨choice h⟩

noncomputable def inhabited_of_exists {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (h : ∃ x, p x) : Inhabited α :=
  inhabited_of_nonempty (Exists.elim h (fun w _ => ⟨w⟩))

/-- All propositions are `Decidable`. -/
noncomputable scoped instance (priority := low) propDecidable (a : Prop) : Decidable a :=
  choice <| match em a with
    | Or.inl h => ⟨isTrue h⟩
    | Or.inr h => ⟨isFalse h⟩

noncomputable def decidableInhabited (a : Prop) : Inhabited (Decidable a) where
  default := inferInstance

instance (a : Prop) : Nonempty (Decidable a) := ⟨propDecidable a⟩

noncomputable def typeDecidableEq (α : Sort u) : DecidableEq α :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

noncomputable def typeDecidable (α : Sort u) : PSum α (α → False) :=
  match (propDecidable (Nonempty α)) with
  | (isTrue hp)  => PSum.inl (@default _ (inhabited_of_nonempty hp))
  | (isFalse hn) => PSum.inr (fun a => absurd (Nonempty.intro a) hn)

noncomputable def strongIndefiniteDescription {α : Sort u} (p : α → Prop) (h : Nonempty α) : {x : α // (∃ y : α, p y) → p x} :=
  @dite _ (∃ x : α, p x) (propDecidable _)
    (fun (hp : ∃ x : α, p x) =>
      show {x : α // (∃ y : α, p y) → p x} from
      let xp := indefiniteDescription _ hp;
      ⟨xp.val, fun _ => xp.property⟩)
    (fun hp => ⟨choice h, fun h => absurd h hp⟩)

/-- the Hilbert epsilon Function -/
noncomputable def epsilon {α : Sort u} [h : Nonempty α] (p : α → Prop) : α :=
  (strongIndefiniteDescription p h).val

theorem epsilon_spec_aux {α : Sort u} (h : Nonempty α) (p : α → Prop) : (∃ y, p y) → p (@epsilon α h p) :=
  (strongIndefiniteDescription p h).property

theorem epsilon_spec {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} (hex : ∃ y, p y) : p (@epsilon α hex.nonempty p) :=
  epsilon_spec_aux hex.nonempty p hex

theorem epsilon_singleton {α : Sort u} (x : α) : @epsilon α ⟨x⟩ (fun y => y = x) = x :=
  @epsilon_spec α (fun y => y = x) ⟨x, rfl⟩

/-- the axiom of choice -/
theorem axiomOfChoice {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {r : ∀ x, β x → Prop} (h : ∀ x, ∃ y, r x y) : ∃ (f : ∀ x, β x), ∀ x, r x (f x) :=
  ⟨_, fun x => choose_spec (h x)⟩

theorem skolem {α : Sort u} {b : α → Sort v} {p : ∀ x, b x → Prop} : (∀ x, ∃ y, p x y) ↔ ∃ (f : ∀ x, b x), ∀ x, p x (f x) :=
  ⟨axiomOfChoice, fun ⟨f, hw⟩ (x) => ⟨f x, hw x⟩⟩

theorem propComplete (a : Prop) : a = True ∨ a = False :=
  match em a with
  | Or.inl ha => Or.inl (eq_true ha)
  | Or.inr hn => Or.inr (eq_false hn)

-- this supersedes byCases in Decidable
theorem byCases {p q : Prop} (hpq : p → q) (hnpq : ¬p → q) : q :=
  Decidable.byCases (dec := propDecidable _) hpq hnpq

-- this supersedes byContradiction in Decidable
theorem byContradiction {p : Prop} (h : ¬p → False) : p :=
  Decidable.byContradiction (dec := propDecidable _) h

/-- The Double Negation Theorem: `¬¬P` is equivalent to `P`.
The left-to-right direction, double negation elimination (DNE),
is classically true but not constructively. -/
@[simp] theorem not_not : ¬¬a ↔ a := Decidable.not_not

/-- Transfer decidability of `¬ p` to decidability of `p`. -/
-- This can not be an instance as it would be tried everywhere.
def decidable_of_decidable_not (p : Prop) [h : Decidable (¬ p)] : Decidable p :=
  match h with
  | isFalse h => isTrue (Classical.not_not.mp h)
  | isTrue h => isFalse h

attribute [local instance] decidable_of_decidable_not in
/-- Negation of the condition `P : Prop` in a `dite` is the same as swapping the branches. -/
@[simp low] protected theorem dite_not [hn : Decidable (¬p)] (x : ¬p → α) (y : ¬¬p → α) :
    dite (¬p) x y = dite p (fun h => y (not_not_intro h)) x := by
  cases hn <;> rename_i g
  · simp [not_not.mp g]
  · simp [g]

attribute [local instance] decidable_of_decidable_not in
/-- Negation of the condition `P : Prop` in a `ite` is the same as swapping the branches. -/
@[simp low] protected theorem ite_not (p : Prop) [Decidable (¬ p)] (x y : α) : ite (¬p) x y = ite p y x :=
  dite_not (fun _ => x) (fun _ => y)

attribute [local instance] decidable_of_decidable_not in
@[simp low] protected theorem decide_not (p : Prop) [Decidable (¬ p)] : decide (¬p) = !decide p :=
  byCases (fun h : p => by simp_all) (fun h => by simp_all)

@[simp low] theorem not_forall {p : α → Prop} : (¬∀ x, p x) ↔ ∃ x, ¬p x := Decidable.not_forall

theorem not_forall_not {p : α → Prop} : (¬∀ x, ¬p x) ↔ ∃ x, p x := Decidable.not_forall_not
theorem not_exists_not {p : α → Prop} : (¬∃ x, ¬p x) ↔ ∀ x, p x := Decidable.not_exists_not

theorem forall_or_exists_not (P : α → Prop) : (∀ a, P a) ∨ ∃ a, ¬ P a := by
  rw [← not_forall]; exact em _
theorem exists_or_forall_not (P : α → Prop) : (∃ a, P a) ∨ ∀ a, ¬ P a := by
  rw [← not_exists]; exact em _

theorem or_iff_not_imp_left  : a ∨ b ↔ (¬a → b) := Decidable.or_iff_not_imp_left
theorem or_iff_not_imp_right : a ∨ b ↔ (¬b → a) := Decidable.or_iff_not_imp_right

theorem not_imp_iff_and_not : ¬(a → b) ↔ a ∧ ¬b := Decidable.not_imp_iff_and_not

theorem not_and_iff_not_or_not : ¬(a ∧ b) ↔ ¬a ∨ ¬b := Decidable.not_and_iff_not_or_not

theorem not_iff : ¬(a ↔ b) ↔ (¬a ↔ b) := Decidable.not_iff

@[simp] theorem imp_iff_left_iff  : (b ↔ a → b) ↔ a ∨ b := Decidable.imp_iff_left_iff
@[simp] theorem imp_iff_right_iff : (a → b ↔ b) ↔ a ∨ b := Decidable.imp_iff_right_iff

@[simp] theorem and_or_imp : a ∧ b ∨ (a → c) ↔ a → b ∨ c := Decidable.and_or_imp

@[simp] theorem not_imp : ¬(a → b) ↔ a ∧ ¬b := Decidable.not_imp_iff_and_not

@[simp] theorem imp_and_neg_imp_iff (p : Prop) {q : Prop} : (p → q) ∧ (¬p → q) ↔ q :=
  Iff.intro (fun (a : _ ∧ _) => (Classical.em p).rec a.left a.right)
            (fun a => And.intro (fun _ => a) (fun _ => a))

end Classical

/- Export for Mathlib compat. -/
export Classical (imp_iff_right_iff imp_and_neg_imp_iff and_or_imp not_imp)

/-- Extract an element from an existential statement, using `Classical.choose`. -/
-- This enables projection notation.
@[reducible] noncomputable def Exists.choose {p : α → Prop} (P : ∃ a, p a) : α := Classical.choose P

/-- Show that an element extracted from `P : ∃ a, p a` using `P.choose` satisfies `p`. -/
theorem Exists.choose_spec {p : α → Prop} (P : ∃ a, p a) : p P.choose := Classical.choose_spec P

grind_pattern Exists.choose_spec => P.choose

/-!
# Coercion

Lean uses a somewhat elaborate system of typeclasses to drive the coercion system.
Here a *coercion* means an invisible function that is automatically inserted
to fix what would otherwise be a type error. For example, if we have:
```
def f (x : Nat) : Int := x
```
then this is clearly not type correct as is, because `x` has type `Nat` but
type `Int` is expected, and normally you will get an error message saying exactly that.
But before it shows that message, it will attempt to synthesize an instance of
`CoeT Nat x Int`, which will end up going through all the other typeclasses defined
below, to discover that there is an instance of `Coe Nat Int` defined.

This instance is defined as:
```
instance : Coe Nat Int := ⟨Int.ofNat⟩
```
so Lean will elaborate the original function `f` as if it said:
```
def f (x : Nat) : Int := Int.ofNat x
```
which is not a type error anymore.

You can also use the `↑` operator to explicitly indicate a coercion. Using `↑x`
instead of `x` in the example will result in the same output.

Because there are many polymorphic functions in Lean, it is often ambiguous where
the coercion can go. For example:
```
def f (x y : Nat) : Int := x + y
```
This could be either `↑x + ↑y` where `+` is the addition on `Int`, or `↑(x + y)`
where `+` is addition on `Nat`, or even `x + y` using a heterogeneous addition
with the type `Nat → Nat → Int`. You can use the `↑` operator to disambiguate
between these possibilities, but generally Lean will elaborate working from the
"outside in", meaning that it will first look at the expression `_ + _ : Int`
and assign the `+` to be the one for `Int`, and then need to insert coercions
for the subterms `↑x : Int` and `↑y : Int`, resulting in the `↑x + ↑y` version.

Note that unlike most operators like `+`, `↑` is always eagerly unfolded at
parse time into its definition. So if we look at the definition of `f` from
before, we see no trace of the `CoeT.coe` function:
```
def f (x : Nat) : Int := x
#print f
-- def f : Nat → Int :=
-- fun (x : Nat) => Int.ofNat x
```

## Important typeclasses

Lean resolves a coercion by either inserting a `CoeDep` instance
or chaining `CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe* CoeTail?` instances.
(That is, zero or one `CoeHead` instances, an arbitrary number of `CoeOut`
instances, etc.)

The `CoeHead? CoeOut*` instances are chained from the "left" side.
So if Lean looks for a coercion from `Nat` to `Int`, it starts by trying coerce
`Nat` using `CoeHead` by looking for a `CoeHead Nat ?α` instance, and then
continuing with `CoeOut`.  Similarly `Coe* CoeTail?` are chained from the "right".

These classes should be implemented for coercions:

* `Coe α β` is the most basic class, and the usual one you will want to use
  when implementing a coercion for your own types.
  The variables in the type `α` must be a subset of the variables in `β`
  (or out-params of type class parameters),
  because `Coe` is chained right-to-left.

* `CoeOut α β` is like `Coe α β` but chained left-to-right.
  Use this if the variables in the type `α` are a superset of the variables in `β`.

* `CoeTail α β` is like `Coe α β`, but only applied once.
  Use this for coercions that would cause loops, like `[Ring R] → CoeTail Nat R`.

* `CoeHead α β` is similar to `CoeOut α β`, but only applied once.
  Use this for coercions that would cause loops, like `[SetLike S α] → CoeHead S (Set α)`.

* `CoeDep α (x : α) β` allows `β` to depend not only on `α` but on the value
  `x : α` itself. This is useful when the coercion function is dependent.
  An example of a dependent coercion is the instance for `Prop → Bool`, because
  it only holds for `Decidable` propositions. It is defined as:
  ```
  instance (p : Prop) [Decidable p] : CoeDep Prop p Bool := ...
  ```

* `CoeFun α (γ : α → Sort v)` is a coercion to a function. `γ a` should be a
  (coercion-to-)function type, and this is triggered whenever an element
  `f : α` appears in an application like `f x` which would not make sense since
  `f` does not have a function type.
  `CoeFun` instances apply to `CoeOut` as well.

* `CoeSort α β` is a coercion to a sort. `β` must be a universe, and this is
  triggered when `a : α` appears in a place where a type is expected, like
  `(x : a)` or `a → a`.
  `CoeSort` instances apply to `CoeOut` as well.

On top of these instances this file defines several auxiliary type classes:
  * `CoeTC := Coe*`
  * `CoeOTC := CoeOut* Coe*`
  * `CoeHTC := CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe*`
  * `CoeHTCT := CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe* CoeTail?`
  * `CoeT := CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe* CoeTail? | CoeDep`

-/

universe u v w w'

/--
`Coe α β` is the typeclass for coercions from `α` to `β`. It can be transitively
chained with other `Coe` instances, and coercion is automatically used when
`x` has type `α` but it is used in a context where `β` is expected.
You can use the `↑x` operator to explicitly trigger coercion.
-/
class Coe (α : semiOutParam (Sort u)) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] Coe.coe

/--
Auxiliary class implementing `Coe*`.
Users should generally not implement this directly.
-/
class CoeTC (α : Sort u) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeTC.coe

instance [Coe β γ] [CoeTC α β] : CoeTC α γ where coe a := Coe.coe (CoeTC.coe a : β)
instance [Coe α β] : CoeTC α β where coe a := Coe.coe a
instance : CoeTC α α where coe a := a

/--
`CoeOut α β` is for coercions that are applied from left-to-right.
-/
class CoeOut (α : Sort u) (β : semiOutParam (Sort v)) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeOut.coe

/--
Auxiliary class implementing `CoeOut* Coe*`.
Users should generally not implement this directly.
-/
class CoeOTC (α : Sort u) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeOTC.coe

instance [CoeOut α β] [CoeOTC β γ] : CoeOTC α γ where coe a := CoeOTC.coe (CoeOut.coe a : β)
instance [CoeTC α β] : CoeOTC α β where coe a := CoeTC.coe a
instance : CoeOTC α α where coe a := a

-- Note: ^^ We add reflexivity instances for CoeOTC/etc. so that we avoid going
-- through a user-defined CoeTC/etc. instance.  (Instances like
-- `CoeTC F (A →+ B)` apply even when the two sides are defeq.)

/--
`CoeHead α β` is for coercions that are applied from left-to-right at most once
at beginning of the coercion chain.
-/
class CoeHead (α : Sort u) (β : semiOutParam (Sort v)) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeHead.coe

/--
Auxiliary class implementing `CoeHead CoeOut* Coe*`.
Users should generally not implement this directly.
-/
class CoeHTC (α : Sort u) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeHTC.coe

instance [CoeHead α β] [CoeOTC β γ] : CoeHTC α γ where coe a := CoeOTC.coe (CoeHead.coe a : β)
instance [CoeOTC α β] : CoeHTC α β where coe a := CoeOTC.coe a
instance : CoeHTC α α where coe a := a

/--
`CoeTail α β` is for coercions that can only appear at the end of a
sequence of coercions. That is, `α` can be further coerced via `Coe σ α` and
`CoeHead τ σ` instances but `β` will only be the expected type of the expression.
-/
class CoeTail (α : semiOutParam (Sort u)) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeTail.coe

/--
Auxiliary class implementing `CoeHead* Coe* CoeTail?`.
Users should generally not implement this directly.
-/
class CoeHTCT (α : Sort u) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
  or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeHTCT.coe

instance [CoeTail β γ] [CoeHTC α β] : CoeHTCT α γ where coe a := CoeTail.coe (CoeHTC.coe a : β)
instance [CoeHTC α β] : CoeHTCT α β where coe a := CoeHTC.coe a
instance : CoeHTCT α α where coe a := a

/--
`CoeDep α (x : α) β` is a typeclass for dependent coercions, that is, the type `β`
can depend on `x` (or rather, the value of `x` is available to typeclass search
so an instance that relates `β` to `x` is allowed).

Dependent coercions do not participate in the transitive chaining process of
regular coercions: they must exactly match the type mismatch on both sides.
-/
class CoeDep (α : Sort u) (_ : α) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- The resulting value of type `β`. The input `x : α` is a parameter to
  the type class, so the value of type `β` may possibly depend on additional
  typeclasses on `x`. -/
  coe : β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeDep.coe

/--
`CoeT` is the core typeclass which is invoked by Lean to resolve a type error.
It can also be triggered explicitly with the notation `↑x` or by double type
ascription `((x : α) : β)`.

A `CoeT` chain has the grammar `CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe* CoeTail? | CoeDep`.
-/
class CoeT (α : Sort u) (_ : α) (β : Sort v) where
  /-- The resulting value of type `β`. The input `x : α` is a parameter to
  the type class, so the value of type `β` may possibly depend on additional
  typeclasses on `x`. -/
  coe : β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeT.coe

instance [CoeHTCT α β] : CoeT α a β where coe := CoeHTCT.coe a
instance [CoeDep α a β] : CoeT α a β where coe := CoeDep.coe a
instance : CoeT α a α where coe := a

/--
`CoeFun α (γ : α → Sort v)` is a coercion to a function. `γ a` should be a
(coercion-to-)function type, and this is triggered whenever an element
`f : α` appears in an application like `f x`, which would not make sense since
`f` does not have a function type.
`CoeFun` instances apply to `CoeOut` as well.
-/
class CoeFun (α : Sort u) (γ : outParam (α → Sort v)) where
  /-- Coerces a value `f : α` to type `γ f`, which should be either be a
  function type or another `CoeFun` type, in order to resolve a mistyped
  application `f x`. -/
  coe : (f : α) → γ f
attribute [coe_decl] CoeFun.coe

instance [CoeFun α fun _ => β] : CoeOut α β where coe a := CoeFun.coe a

/--
`CoeSort α β` is a coercion to a sort. `β` must be a universe, and this is
triggered when `a : α` appears in a place where a type is expected, like
`(x : a)` or `a → a`.
`CoeSort` instances apply to `CoeOut` as well.
-/
class CoeSort (α : Sort u) (β : outParam (Sort v)) where
  /-- Coerces a value of type `α` to `β`, which must be a universe. -/
  coe : α → β
attribute [coe_decl] CoeSort.coe

instance [CoeSort α β] : CoeOut α β where coe a := CoeSort.coe a

/--
`↑x` represents a coercion, which converts `x` of type `α` to type `β`, using
typeclasses to resolve a suitable conversion function. You can often leave the
`↑` off entirely, since coercion is triggered implicitly whenever there is a
type error, but in ambiguous cases it can be useful to use `↑` to disambiguate
between e.g. `↑x + ↑y` and `↑(x + y)`.
-/
syntax:1024 (name := coeNotation) "↑" term:1024 : term

/-- `⇑ t` coerces `t` to a function. -/
syntax:1024 (name := coeFunNotation) "⇑" term:1024 : term

/-- `↥ t` coerces `t` to a type. -/
syntax:1024 (name := coeSortNotation) "↥" term:1024 : term

/-! # Basic instances -/

instance boolToProp : Coe Bool Prop where
  coe b := Eq b true

instance boolToSort : CoeSort Bool Prop where
  coe b := b

instance decPropToBool (p : Prop) [Decidable p] : CoeDep Prop p Bool where
  coe := decide p

instance subtypeCoe {α : Sort u} {p : α → Prop} : CoeOut (Subtype p) α where
  coe v := v.val

/-! # Coe bridge -/

/--
Helper definition used by the elaborator. It is not meant to be used directly by users.

This is used for coercions between monads, in the case where we want to apply
a monad lift and a coercion on the result type at the same time.
-/
@[coe_decl] abbrev Lean.Internal.liftCoeM {m : Type u → Type v} {n : Type u → Type w} {α β : Type u}
    [MonadLiftT m n] [∀ a, CoeT α a β] [Monad n] (x : m α) : n β := do
  let a ← liftM x
  pure (CoeT.coe a)

/--
Helper definition used by the elaborator. It is not meant to be used directly by users.

This is used for coercing the result type under a monad.
-/
@[coe_decl] abbrev Lean.Internal.coeM {m : Type u → Type v} {α β : Type u}
    [∀ a, CoeT α a β] [Monad m] (x : m α) : m β := do
  let a ← x
  pure (CoeT.coe a)

prelude
